subject: Weekly sprint capacity forecasting check-in: commits vs. asks
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly sprint capacity forecasting check-in: commits vs. asks

Team — kicking off this week's cross-functional capacity check for StellarRetail (DEAL-8731). Quick context: Stella's close motion accelerated last week and sales added two additional GA-focused SKUs into their expected Q4 consumption profile. I attached the latest pipeline snapshot and a couple of capacity scenarios.

Asks for this week: 
- Laura: confirm whether the 1.2k token/sec SLA in the scenario sheet maps to the same pool we planned last month (named "northstar-dedicated-1"). If not, call it out.
- Karthik: can infra absorb a +25% burst for 6 weeks if we reserve 2 additional A100s in the northern pool? Please include latency SLO impact if we keep current batching thresholds.
- Ben/Marissa: finance — what's the rough headroom for a mid-quarter top-up if Stellar signs an accelerated commit? I need a provisional $ delta by EOD Wed so sales can scope discounts.

Note: I've highlighted two risk paths in capacity_scenarios_3x.pdf — one where latency climbs above 300ms under concurrent eval workloads and one where we need additional prefix cache tuning. If any of you want a short sync, I'm free Wed 10–11am PT.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: 2026-08-09_weekly_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly sprint capacity forecasting check-in: commits vs. asks

Thanks Camila — reviewed the workbook. Short answers: 
- The "northstar-dedicated-1" pool in the sheet is the same pool we earmarked for Stellar in July; capacity numbers align with what infra reported then (pool_id: northstar-1).
- The 1.2k token/sec target assumes current quantization profile (q4_0) and no aggressive batching; if we enable conservative batching we can increase throughput ~18% but latency median improves only marginally.

I linked a quick notes doc in Drive (see related_links) and updated a tab called "stella_sla_mapping" in the snapshot. Two operational notes: 
1) We currently have 8% spare headroom in northstar-1 across on-peak windows; that is before any burst slots.
2) If Karthik confirms the additional A100s, we should still run a week of pre-roll smoke tests to validate the KV cache behavior with Stellar's 2-token prefix pattern.

I'll be on Wed 10:30am PT for the sync.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
(Attachment referenced: capacity_scenarios_3x.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly sprint capacity forecasting check-in: commits vs. asks

Short infra readout: 
- 2 additional A100s in northstar-1 for a 6-week reservation window is feasible from a provisioning perspective but it requires bumping the pool's machine class which will change baseline cost by ~14% (see quick calc below).
- Latency: if we keep current batching thresholds (+ KV cache warmup) we expect p95 to stay under 320ms in the +25% burst scenario. The real risk is concurrent eval workloads from other teams — we'd need an isolation policy or soft quota to maintain tight p95.
- Ops action: I'll raise a provisioning ticket (PROV-1129) once finance signs off on the mid-quarter top-up. ETA for procurement + boot is ~72 hours after ticket approval; smoke tests need an extra 48 hours.

Quick cost calc (back-of-envelope): additional A100s (2 · spot-equivalent) ≈ +$28k/month incremental; for 6 weeks that's ~$42k. If you want formal finops numbers, Marissa should confirm committed vs. one-off budget.

-Karthik
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly sprint capacity forecasting check-in: commits vs. asks

Quick finance take: 
- We can cover a one-time 6-week top-up for Stellar under our mid-quarter flexibility pool up to $50k without escalated approval. That covers Karthik's $42k estimate with a small buffer.
- If Stellar requests a rebate/discount for the top-up, we need to see the final ARR uplift projection. For anything >$50k we need a VP-level approval and a short business justification.

Action items for Ben/Camila: please send the finalized uplift projection by EOD Wed so I can lock the one-time allocation. Also include whether they want burst credits or reserved capacity — that affects how we book the spend.

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
(Attachment referenced: MVP_prefix_cache_accounting.csv)

From: Samantha Torres <sam.torres@stellarretail.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@stellarretail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly sprint capacity forecasting check-in: commits vs. asks

Camila / Ben — thanks for the transparency and quick turnaround. On our side: 
- We can confirm an accelerated partial commit covering estimated Q4 eval traffic that maps to ~1.5k token/sec steady-state and a 6-week peak strategy that matches the +25% burst ask.
- We're prepared to sign a short amendment for a one-time top-up and will provide the uplift projection (ARR delta) in the amendment draft by Mon 16 Aug.

Appreciate the flexibility on finance here. Please proceed with provisional provisioning after Marissa confirms allocation; we'll sign the amendment once legal runs a quick redline.

— Samantha Torres
VP of Platform Engineering
StellarRetail
(External: ops@stellarretail.com)
